intent_contract.text: 반영한 키워드가 이미지에 실제로 반영되는지까지 테스트할 수 있는 랜덤한 복잡한 컨셉

The requester asks for an independent random complex photo test using the attachment, then checks actual image realization. The theater repair role, adult ages, snapped-braid event, two-person staging, opposing hand surfaces, self/other garment contact, sidelong lens glance and crop are agent-owned test-design choices. WHO is an attentive adult craft worker whose slight inviting smile supports sensual=1 while precise repair dominates. WHERE is a tactile backstage workshop. HOW is a nearby observer acknowledged by a glance. WHY NOW is the stopped beat after a braid snapped and snagged the apron. Compared with an isolated tool portrait and a fully busy downward-looking repair, this two-person paused repair makes ownership and contrasting hand surfaces legible. Face/hair reference appearance supplies no biography, age, identity, personality or body-shape inference.

An intricate photographic scene captures a single visible action in a theatrical costume repair room. The central seamstress is a newly designed 32-year-old woman; her visible face and hair follow the supplied image: a dark chin-length bob, separated wispy fringe, dark eyes, softly tapered jaw and softly rounded lips. She stands on screen left beside a workbench, wearing a sage cotton work shirt, an ivory canvas apron and charcoal trousers. A newly designed 38-year-old male stage performer stands on screen right in a plum velvet cape over a dark jacket. She is separating a snapped gold braided cord on his cape from the top edge of her own apron, holding the interrupted repair for one attentive beat. Her right thumb and index finger pinch the top canvas edge of her own apron at her upper chest, making a small raised fold; the inner surface of her right palm and its creases face the camera. Her left forearm reaches toward the performer, and her left index finger curves visibly beneath the gold braid where it remains attached to his upper lapel. The back of her left hand faces the lens, displaying its knuckles and short nails while its palm faces his jacket. A small star brooch sits above two short frayed cord ends hanging on his cape. Her shoulders remain nearly frontal, her head turns modestly toward him, and her eyes glance back toward the lens. An asymmetric closed-mouth smile gives this brief professional pause a quietly inviting presence. Both of her wrists and connected forearms remain visible between the separate contact sites. A landscape frame includes both adult heads through upper hips; the apron clearly belongs to her and the cape stays worn by him. Warm task-lamp light falls across her face and the two hands, with garment racks and a spool tray softly receding behind them. Crisp canvas folds, velvet nap and metal glints keep the repair tactile within a restrained backstage editorial photograph.

definitions.principle: These creative definitions guide agent-owned choices within requester meaning, not clinical classifications. Zero/off disables added treatment, never removes explicitly requested content or artistic judgment. Expression levels describe prominence in the whole image; creativity levels describe interpretive freedom. Neither measures exposure percentages, detail quotas, quality scores, or native image-model parameters. Intensity and expression are separate choices; higher intensity does not prescribe a garment, material or expression category. Creativity leaves style, extra props and surreal treatment open to the request and artistic judgment. Emphasis directs only active sensual and fetish axes without changing their intensities. Popular permits familiar appeal without requiring trend search; overt is an available expression, not the mandatory meaning of level three. Choose a coherent expression suited to this particular scene. Sensual and fetish may share the same expressive choice.

sensual.definition: Broadly interpreted human attraction and desire, including everyday, popular, intimate, suggestive, seductive, and overt expressions.

levels.0: No added sensual treatment; preserve explicitly requested content.
levels.1: This expression is a subtle supporting quality.
levels.2: This expression is clearly readable in the image.
levels.3: This expression leads the image's appeal and direction.

fetish.definition: Sexual attraction or arousal focused on particular objects, bodily features, clothing, materials, roles, situations, behaviors, or sensory qualities that carry special erotic significance, interpreted broadly beyond conventional fetish aesthetics.

levels.0: No added fetish treatment; preserve explicitly requested content.
levels.1: This focus is a subtle supporting quality.
levels.2: This focus is clearly readable in the image.
levels.3: This focus leads the image's appeal and direction.

adult_appeal_emphasis.definition: Relative leadership of the active sensual and fetish axes within one coherent expression.

choice_descriptions.auto: Let the higher effective intensity lead; equal active intensities share leadership. Add no emphasis when both axes are inactive.
choice_descriptions.sensual_led: Let broad attraction and desire lead, with any active distinctive fascination supporting the expression.
choice_descriptions.balanced: Give both active axes comparable influence within one coherent expression; separate styling details are not required.
choice_descriptions.fetish_led: Let the distinctive focus of attraction or fascination lead, with any active sensual expression supporting it.

creativity.definition: Freedom to interpret unspecified choices and explore relationships within the request.

levels.0: Realize the request directly, filling only what is needed for a coherent image.
levels.1: Introduce restrained variations close to the requested direction.
levels.2: Actively reinterpret open choices into a coherent authorial direction.
levels.3: Boldly explore unexpected relationships and interpretations while preserving the request's core meaning.

viewer_experience.definition: Expose the detailed viewer-experience review when enabled. Always consider the intended impression in interpreted_intent, even when this additional review is off.

reference_edit_mode.definition: Use the selected reference-edit workflow only within the requester's reference-use scope. Record that scope in the core; a face/hair reference does not lock clothing, body shape or composition and does not prove identity. Off does not discard a supplied reference.

surreal.definition: Added departures from ordinary reality, interpreted broadly across space, scale, causality, materials, and atmosphere, including dreamlike, uncanny, symbolic, and impossible relationships.

levels.0: No added surreal treatment; preserve explicitly requested fantasy and impossible elements.
levels.1: Surreal qualities are a subtle supporting presence.
levels.2: Surreal qualities are clearly readable in the image.
levels.3: Surreal qualities lead the image's main impression and direction; a single coherent relationship may carry this prominence.

trend_layer.definition: Consider the chosen treatment from the initial composition. Refine it later without adding it twice. Off does not remove a treatment explicitly present in the request.

emphasis_resolution.reason: Effective sensual=1, fetish=0; the higher intensity leads.

authorial_core.baseline_prompt_en: An intricate photographic scene captures a single visible action in a theatrical costume repair room. The central seamstress is a newly designed 32-year-old woman; her visible face and hair follow the supplied image: a dark chin-length bob, separated wispy fringe, dark eyes, softly tapered jaw and softly rounded lips. She stands on screen left beside a workbench, wearing a sage cotton work shirt, an ivory canvas apron and charcoal trousers. A newly designed 38-year-old male stage performer stands on screen right in a plum velvet cape over a dark jacket. She is separating a snapped gold braided cord on his cape from the top edge of her own apron, holding the interrupted repair for one attentive beat. Her right thumb and index finger pinch the top canvas edge of her own apron at her upper chest, making a small raised fold; the inner surface of her right palm and its creases face the camera. Her left forearm reaches toward the performer, and her left index finger curves visibly beneath the gold braid where it remains attached to his upper lapel. The back of her left hand faces the lens, displaying its knuckles and short nails while its palm faces his jacket. A small star brooch sits above two short frayed cord ends hanging on his cape. Her shoulders remain nearly frontal, her head turns modestly toward him, and her eyes glance back toward the lens. An asymmetric closed-mouth smile gives this brief professional pause a quietly inviting presence. Both of her wrists and connected forearms remain visible between the separate contact sites. A landscape frame includes both adult heads through upper hips; the apron clearly belongs to her and the cape stays worn by him. Warm task-lamp light falls across her face and the two hands, with garment racks and a spool tray softly receding behind them. Crisp canvas folds, velvet nap and metal glints keep the repair tactile within a restrained backstage editorial photograph.
